title: 5.10.9 Check: Enemies and waves
description: Six multiple-choice questions on parallel arrays, the nested hit loop and its break, waves that wait for a clear field, and what one more enemy fact costs. Checked instantly.

questions.question: `enemies[2]`, `enemyHp[2]` and `enemyWorth[2]`: what do they have in common?
options: They were made on the same frame
questions.explanation: In parallel arrays the index is the glue: index 2 in all three arrays is one enemy's sprite, hp and worth.

questions.question: 5 shots and 4 enemies are alive. At most how many overlap tests does `hitEnemies()` make this frame?
questions.explanation: The outer loop takes each of the 5 shots and the inner loop tries it on each of the 4 enemies, so 5 times 4 is 20; a break after a hit can only make it fewer.

questions.question: Why does the inner loop `break` right after a shot hits?
options: That shot has been spliced out, so `bullets[i]` is now a different shot or `undefined`
questions.explanation: The shot at index i is gone, so reading `bullets[i]` again would test another shot twice or ask `undefined` for `.overlaps`; break leaves only the inner loop.

questions.question: Why does `nextWave()` start with `if (enemies.length > 0) return;`?
options: The pause only counts while the field is clear, so waves cannot pile up
questions.explanation: Returning while any enemy is left means the pause only counts down on a clear field, so a new wave never lands on top of the last one.

questions.question: The landing code splices `enemies` and `enemyWorth` but not `enemyHp`. What do you see?
options: Later enemies read the wrong hp: their labels and the shots they need disagree
questions.explanation: After a landing `enemyHp` is one item longer than the other two, so later enemies read a neighbour's hp: a crimson 1 can take three shots and an orange 3 die in one.

questions.question: You want each enemy to have a shield value too. In this Part B code, what has to change?
options: A new array, a push in `spawnEnemy`, a splice in both removal places, a line in `startRound`, and the line that uses it
questions.explanation: A fact kept in its own parallel array needs the array, a push, a splice in every place an enemy is removed, a reset in startRound, and the code that reads it.
